structured_result.summary: Focused review of the packaging alias correction at /private/tmp/task-runners-alias-fix-tw3zg1ce. scripts/package.sh no longer changes into the repository root. It computes the root only to build an absolute xtask manifest path and runs `cargo run --manifest-path <root>/xtask/Cargo.toml --package xtask -- package "$@"`, so a relative --binary now resolves from the caller's working directory, as the README states. The previously reported P3 relative-path error is resolved. Internal cargo metadata and build calls still set current_dir(root), so release builds are unaffected. The new test runs the real script from an external directory whose path contains spaces, with a mock cargo on PATH. It verifies the preserved physical cwd, the absolute manifest path, the verbatim forwarded options, and that the relative binary resolves from the caller. No concrete new regression was found.
coverage: CHANGES.diff in full (scripts/package.sh and the new xtask test)
scripts/package.sh as fixed: root computation, no cd, exec cargo run with absolute xtask manifest path, quoted "$@" forwarding

xtask/src/main.rs:320-479: run() root derivation from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, unchanged select_binary call path, parse test, and package_script_preserves_external_cwd_and_relative_binary_argument (mock cargo, external cwd with spaces, expected argv and cwd, relative binary resolved and read from the caller's cwd)
limitations: No commands, tests or builds were run; the parent-reported xtask test results and manual script invocation are relied upon.

Test fragility, not a product bug: the script computes task_runners_root with logical `pwd` (not -P), while the test compares against root.join("xtask/Cargo.toml").canonicalize(). If CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR ever contains a symlinked component, the expected and actual manifest paths could differ and the test could fail spuriously.

Because cargo now starts in the caller's cwd, caller-side .cargo/config.toml or rust-toolchain.toml files in that directory or its parents affect compiling and running xtask itself. The checkout's .cargo/config.toml only defined the alias, and xtask's own cargo metadata/build calls still use current_dir(root), so no concrete regression was identified.
Did not verify Cargo-version-specific behavior of combining --manifest-path with --package xtask.
The new test mocks cargo and does not exercise the real xtask packaging end to end through the script; that path is covered only by the parent's manual invocation.
Did not re-read other files; per the brief they are unchanged from the previously reviewed candidate.
